screening_decisions.reason: RCT comparing LMWH (nadroparin) to placebo in ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy for metastatic/locally advanced solid cancer. Primary outcome was VTE events. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT comparing dalteparin (LMWH) added to chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone in SCLC patients. Although primary outcome was survival, it compares anticoagulant to no anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
RCT comparing warfarin + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone in SCLC patients. Compares oral anticoagulant to no anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
RCT comparing enoxaparin (LMWH) added to standard treatment vs standard treatment alone in SCLC patients. VTE incidence was a secondary outcome. Meets selection criteria.

Phase II trial with 3 dalteparin dose groups but NO control group (no placebo or no treatment arm). Abstract explicitly states 'The lack of control group precluded any inference on the antineoplastic effect of dalteparin.' Does not meet selection criteria requiring comparison to no thromboprophylaxis or placebo.

Study population is pediatric (age 1-18 years) with acute lymphoblastic leukemia receiving induction therapy. The review focuses on ambulatory cancer patients, and pediatric ALL patients undergoing induction are typically hospitalized, not ambulatory. Population does not match review scope.

Two double-blind RCTs (TOPIC-1 and TOPIC-2) comparing certoparin (LMWH) to placebo in ambulatory patients with metastatic breast cancer or stage III/IV lung cancer. Primary outcome was VTE. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT comparing dalteparin (LMWH) to placebo in patients with advanced malignancy. While primary outcome was survival, VTE rates were reported. Conservative inclusion as it compares anticoagulant to placebo in cancer patients.
RCT comparing dalteparin to observation (no thromboprophylaxis) in ambulatory cancer patients at high VTE risk starting a new systemic regimen. Primary outcome was VTE. Meets selection criteria.

Double-blind RCT comparing nadroparin (LMWH) to placebo in patients with metastasized or locally advanced solid tumors. While primary outcome was survival, it compares anticoagulant to placebo in cancer patients. Conservative inclusion.
RCT comparing two different anticoagulants (aspirin vs enoxaparin) in multiple myeloma patients receiving lenalidomide-based therapy. Meets criteria for comparing two different anticoagulants.
RCT comparing subcutaneous heparin to no heparin in SCLC patients receiving chemotherapy. Compares anticoagulant to no anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
RCT comparing bemiparin (LMWH) added to chemoradiotherapy vs chemoradiotherapy alone in SCLC patients. Compares anticoagulant to no anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
Double-blind RCT comparing very-low-dose warfarin to placebo in women receiving chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer. Primary outcome was thromboembolic events. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing apixaban (oral anticoagulant) at different doses to placebo in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. Secondary outcome included VTE. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing LMWH added to standard treatment vs standard treatment alone in lung cancer patients. VTE-free survival was a secondary outcome. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing dalteparin (LMWH) added to gemcitabine vs gemcitabine alone in pancreatic cancer patients. Primary endpoint was VTE reduction. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing warfarin to no warfarin in SCLC patients receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Compares oral anticoagulant to no anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.

Study population is pediatric (children with ALL) receiving L-asparaginase. The review focuses on ambulatory cancer patients, and pediatric ALL patients are not the target population. Population does not match review scope.
RCT comparing three different anticoagulants (aspirin, warfarin, enoxaparin) in multiple myeloma patients receiving thalidomide-based regimens. Meets criteria for comparing different anticoagulants.

RCT comparing enoxaparin (LMWH) vs observation (chemotherapy alone) in ambulatory patients with advanced pancreatic cancer receiving first-line chemotherapy. Primary outcomes include symptomatic VTE reduction. Meets all selection criteria.

While this is an RCT of dalteparin vs placebo, the population consists of patients with newly diagnosed malignant glioma starting treatment within 4 weeks of surgery. These are post-surgical brain tumor patients, not ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy as specified in the review protocol.

RCT comparing LMWH vs standard care/placebo in patients with advanced cancer. Although the primary endpoint was overall survival, VTE rates were reported as secondary outcomes. Conservative inclusion warranted given it is an RCT of anticoagulant in cancer patients.

RCT comparing nadroparin vs no treatment in patients with advanced cancer (NSCLC, prostate, pancreatic). Primary outcome was survival, but bleeding events were reported. Conservative inclusion as it is an RCT of anticoagulant in cancer patients.

RCT comparing warfarin vs control in patients with small cell lung cancer receiving combination chemotherapy plus radiation therapy. Although primary outcome was survival, this is an RCT of oral anticoagulant in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
Phase II RCT comparing enoxaparin vs observation in advanced cancer patients. VTE cumulative incidence was the primary outcome. Meets selection criteria for RCT of anticoagulant in cancer patients.

Double-blind RCT comparing semuloparin (ultra-LMWH) vs placebo in patients with metastatic or locally advanced solid tumors beginning chemotherapy. Primary efficacy outcome was VTE composite. Perfect match for selection criteria.

Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of apixaban vs placebo in ambulatory cancer patients at intermediate-to-high risk initiating chemotherapy. Primary outcome was objectively documented VTE. Perfect match for selection criteria.
Double-blind RCT comparing rivaroxaban vs placebo in high-risk ambulatory cancer patients. Primary endpoint was VTE composite. Perfect match for selection criteria.

Abstract contains only a figure caption about SCLC survival with hazard ratios. No information about study design, intervention, or whether this is an RCT. Insufficient information to assess eligibility.

RCT of tinzaparin vs no treatment in patients with completely resected stage I-IIIA NSCLC. This is an adjuvant/post-surgical setting, not ambulatory patients receiving chemotherapy. Primary outcome was overall survival (anti-tumor effect), not VTE prophylaxis.

Phase 2 clinical trial where aspirin was added to the regimen during the study, creating three retrospective groups based on timing of aspirin initiation. This is not a randomized controlled trial - groups were not prospectively randomized.

Compares vena cava filter placement vs conservative therapy in cancer patients undergoing surgery and/or polychemotherapy. Population is not clearly ambulatory (includes surgical patients). Abstract lacks clear indication of randomization.

RCT of nadroparin vs control in patients with completely resected NSCLC. This is an adjuvant/post-surgical setting, not ambulatory patients receiving chemotherapy. Primary outcome was recurrence-free survival, not VTE prophylaxis.

Subgroup analysis of CERTIFY trial comparing certoparin vs UFH in acutely-ill, non-surgical patients ≥70 years. Population is hospitalized acutely-ill patients, not ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.

RCT of intermittent pneumatic compression in postoperative setting. Population includes both patients with and without malignant disease, and the setting is postoperative, not ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
Observational study comparing patients who received LMWH prophylaxis vs those who did not. Groups were compared based on practice of thromboprophylaxis, not prospective randomization. Not an RCT.
Prospective cohort study with noncontemporaneous control group, not an RCT. Additionally, population is children with ALL, not adult ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
Describes three series of MM patients receiving aspirin - this is an observational case series report, not a randomized controlled trial. No randomization described.
This is an economic evaluation/cost analysis of a previous RCT, not a primary RCT itself. Does not provide original clinical trial data for screening purposes.

This study does not meet the selection criteria. The population is patients with knee osteoarthritis, not cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. The intervention is transcutaneous electrostimulation for pain control, not anticoagulant or mechanical thromboprophylaxis. The outcome is pain and adverse events, not venous thromboembolism. This study is completely off-topic for the review question.

This study does not meet the selection criteria. First, it is an observational cohort study using registry data (Danish National Registry of Patients, Danish Cancer Registry, Danish Mortality Files), not a randomised controlled trial. Second, the study focuses on prognosis of cancer in patients with VTE, not on primary thromboprophylaxis interventions. There is no intervention being tested - it is a prognostic study comparing survival outcomes between cancer patients with and without VTE.

This study does not meet the selection criteria. While the population (cancer patients receiving chemotherapy) is relevant, this is not a randomised controlled trial of an intervention. This paper describes the development and validation of a modified risk assessment score (the Protecht score) for VTE risk stratification. Although it references the Protecht study (NCT 00951574) which tested nadroparin prophylaxis, this publication itself is about risk score methodology, not an RCT comparing anticoagulant interventions to placebo/no prophylaxis or comparing two anticoagulants.
